en: Udāna 4.4 Yakkhapahārasutta Thus have I heard:
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna were dwelling at Kapotakandara.
On that occasion, during a bright night, with his hair recently shorn, the Venerable Sāriputta was sitting in the open air, having attained a certain state of concentration.
Now at that time, two yakṣas who were friends were traveling from the northern direction toward the southern direction on some business.
Those yakṣas saw the Venerable Sāriputta sitting in the open air during a moonlit night with his hair recently shorn.
Having seen him, one yakṣa said this to the second yakṣa:
“It occurs to me, friend, to strike this ascetic on the head.
When this was said, that yakkha said this to the other yakkha:
“Enough, friend; do not attack the ascetic.”
“Exalted, friend, is that ascetic; he is of great psychic power and great majesty.
A second time, that yakkha said this to the other yakkha:
“It occurs to me, friend, to give a blow to the head of this ascetic.”
A second time, that yakkha said this to the other yakkha:
"Enough, friend; do not attack the ascetic.
That ascetic, friend, is sublime, possessed of great psychic power and great majesty."
A third time, that yakkha said this to the other yakkha:
"It occurs to me, friend, to give a blow to the head of this ascetic.
A third time, that yakkha said this to the other yakkha:
“Enough, friend, do not insult the ascetic.
That ascetic, friend, is sublime, possessed of great psychic power and great majesty.
But that yakkha, disregarding the other yakkha, struck the head of the Venerable Elder Sāriputta.
That blow was indeed mighty; by such a blow one might have felled a nāga seven or seven-and-a-half cubits high, or shattered a great mountain peak.
Yet that yakkha, crying out, "I am burning! I am burning!", fell right there into the Great Hell.
With his purified divine eye, which surpasses the human, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna saw that yakkha dealing the blow to the head of the Elder Venerable Sāriputta.
Having seen him, he approached the Venerable Sāriputta; having approached, he said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:
"I hope you are bearing up, friend; I hope you are getting by; I hope you have no great suffering?
"I am bearing up, friend Moggallāna; I am getting by, friend Moggallāna."
“Moreover, my head is slightly pained.
“It is wonderful, friend Sāriputta! It is marvelous, friend Sāriputta!
To what an extent the Venerable Sāriputta is of great psychic power and great majesty!”
"In this case, friend Sāriputta, a certain yakkha struck you on the head.
That blow was so great that it could have felled a nāga seven or seven-and-a-half cubits high, or shattered a massive mountain peak; yet the Venerable Sāriputta said:
‘It is bearable for me, friend Moggallāna; it is endurable for me, friend Moggallāna.’"
"Moreover, my head is slightly pained.
"It is wonderful, friend Moggallāna; it is marvelous, friend Moggallāna!
How great is the psychic power and majesty of the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, that he can even see a *yakkha*!"
"But now we do not even see a dust-demon.
With his purified divine ear-element, which surpasses the human, the Blessed One heard this conversation between those two great beings.
Then the Blessed One, having understood the significance of this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation (udāna):
“He whose mind is like a rock,
steady and unshaken,
detached from things that cause passion— ”
He does not become angry with those who deserve anger;
for one whose mind is thus developed,
how could suffering come to him?
The fourth.
